issues.legal_issue: An earlier testamentary disposition of property remained effective when a later clause referred to the property in a different adoption contingency.
material_facts: The testator's will gave a daughter a life interest in the disputed property and provided that the property would pass after her death to another daughter and her children, subject to a payment to the life tenant's child.
A later clause stated that the life tenant would enjoy the property as described earlier, but did not repeat the remainder disposition.
The widow adopted a son of one of the testator's nephews, and the will contained no express alteration of the earlier disposition of the disputed property for that contingency.

The will made family provisions in its earlier paragraphs and specified modifications for the different adoption contingencies; it did not indicate that the earlier family provisions were cancelled when a nephew's son was adopted.

The trial court accepted the interpretation that the earlier remainder disposition applied, while the appellate court held that the later clause alone governed and allowed the adopted son's claim as heir.
issues.conclusion: The earlier disposition remained operative under the adoption contingency that occurred, so the property passed to the designated daughter and her children after the life tenant's death, subject to the stated payment. The appeal was allowed and the trial court's decree was restored.
issues.legal_principle: A will must be construed as a whole to ascertain the testator's intention primarily from its language, with surrounding circumstances used as an aid to understanding that language; a court must give effect to the intention expressed and may not add to the testamentary dispositions. Under Venkata Narasimha v. Parthasarthy, the court may consider the testator's circumstances and relationships in construing the document. A presumption against intestacy may be used only where the context or surrounding circumstances justify it and there is genuine ambiguity; it does not permit plain words to be given an unnatural meaning, as stated in Re Edwards; Jones v. Jones. The court concluded that it was unnecessary to rely on that presumption here.

rule.if: testamentary_construction_appeal and earlier_family_bequest_covers_property and later_clause_refers_to_only_part_of_bequest and no_express_change_to_remainder and will_scheme_applies_family_gifts_across_contingencies and different_adoption_contingency_occurred

predicates.testamentary_construction_appeal: A party appealed a judgment that construed a testamentary document disposing of property.
predicates.earlier_family_bequest_covers_property: The testator earlier disposed of the property by granting a life interest and designating who would take afterward.
predicates.later_clause_refers_to_only_part_of_bequ: A later clause refers to the earlier life interest without repeating the disposition of the remaining interest.
predicates.no_express_change_to_remainder: The testator made no express alteration to the earlier disposition of the remaining interest for the relevant contingency.
predicates.will_scheme_applies_family_gifts_across_: The testamentary document's structure shows that family gifts made earlier were intended to apply across the different contingencies it describes.
predicates.different_adoption_contingency_occurred: The adoption contingency that occurred differed from the one associated with the original principal disposition.

issues.definition: When a testamentary-construction appeal concerns an earlier family bequest that covers the property, a later clause refers only to part of that bequest, no express change is made to the remainder, the will's scheme applies family gifts across contingencies, and a different adoption contingency occurs, the earlier remainder disposition remains effective.
